title: Genomic predisposition is associated with the direction of sex chromosome evolution.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: No data file was opened because none was reachable. I checked: Europe PMC core record (isOpenAccess=N, inPMC=N, hasSuppl=N, no text-mined accessions), NCBI elink from PubMed 42658954 (no GEO/SRA/BioProject/BioSample/dbGaP links at all), NCBI assembly search for Gekkota (54 assemblies, submitters are Iridian Genomes, Milwaukee Public Museum, Sanger, USC, etc. - none traceable to this paper's BGI/Sun Yat-sen group), NCBI GEO search for Gekkota (108 series, none matching this study), Zenodo and figshare searches, and two direct HEAD requests to Science supplementary-file URLs (both HTTP 403 Forbidden). The article landing page is also 403. One candidate assembly, GCA_051903775.2 (Gekko kuhli, chromosome level), sits in BioProject PRJNA746349 from co-author Tony Gamble's museum, but that is a long-standing lab umbrella project, not a deposit identifiable with this paper.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Everything about the content: 19-22 gecko genomes, 22 sex chromosome systems traced to 16-17 ancestral chromosomes, 11 datable origins, the testis-enriched -> ZW / testis-depleted -> XY association, the extension across 39 vertebrate species, and the dosage-balance result. All of this comes from the abstract plus the EurekAlert press release; I could read neither the methods, the data availability statement, nor any supplementary table.

a1_downloadable.note: FAIL. The paper is paywalled with no PubMed Central copy, so there is no data availability statement to read and no supplementary tables to open; direct requests to the Science supplement return HTTP 403. Searches of Europe PMC accessions, NCBI links from the PubMed record, NCBI assembly/GEO/BioProject, Zenodo and figshare found no deposit attributable to this study. The analysis tables that carry the labels (ancestral chromosome assignment per sex chromosome origin, testis-enrichment per region, male/female expression ratios) exist only in that supplement.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Not reached in the files, but near-certainly a fail on the checklist's own definition: the prediction target - 'did this ancestral chromosome region become XY or ZW' - is an inference produced by whole-genome synteny reconstruction plus phylogenetic dating across 19-22 species, not a column sitting in a released table. Even with the supplement in hand, the feature side (ancestral gene content, testis-enrichment) would have to be rebuilt from genome alignments and RNA-seq.

a3_inputs_present.note: Not verified. Inputs would be chromosome-level genome assemblies and testis RNA-seq, none of which I could locate as public files tied to this paper; raw sequencing is also excluded by project policy and genome-scale alignment is outside the laptop budget.

a4_units_stated.note: Unknown - no table seen. The paper's quantities (gene counts, expression fold-enrichment, divergence times in millions of years) are the sort that are usually stated, but I verified nothing.

a5_enough_rows.note: FAIL independently of access. The unit of analysis for the headline claim is a sex chromosome origin event: the press release says 22 sex chromosome systems in 20 gecko species from 17 ancestral chromosomes, with 11 datable origins, and the cross-amniote extension covers 39 vertebrate species. That is tens of labelled examples against the checklist's ~400 minimum for classification. Per-gene or per-window rows would be pseudoreplicates of the same ~22 events.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Not assessed in files. Supplementary tables would be small, but any honest redo of the features needs multi-species whole-genome synteny, which is not a 16 GB laptop task.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: FAIL on consistency of the only two public descriptions: the abstract says 19 geckos and 16 ancestral chromosomes, while the institutional press release says 22 gecko species (plus 2 outgroups), 22 sex chromosome systems in 20 species and 17 ancestral chromosomes. With no download to arbitrate, I cannot tell which is right.

a8_label_provenance.note: The XY-versus-ZW label itself traces to real cytogenetic and sequencing evidence, which is fine, but the ancestral-state assignment is the output of a phylogenetic reconstruction, i.e. a model's inference, and the 'testis-enriched' feature and the 'direction' label are both derived from the same comparative genomic reconstruction - exactly the leakage-by-construction pattern A8 warns about.

honest_claim_h3: No claim is supportable: with roughly 22 independent sex chromosome origins and no accessible table of them, any model of 'which direction a chromosome evolves' would be fitting tens of correlated data points.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use an ancestral chromosome's gene content to predict whether it becomes a male-determining (XY) or female-determining (ZW) sex chromosome.
plain_idea.train_on: One row per independent origin of a sex chromosome, described by the genes the ancestral chromosome carried (notably how many are switched on mainly in testis). The paper covers about 22 such origins in geckos and extends the pattern to 39 vertebrate species; I verified none of these counts in a file.
plain_idea.predict: A two-way label: XY (male is the one with two different sex chromosomes) versus ZW (female is). The true answer comes from karyotyping and sequencing of males and females in each species, as reported in the paper.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Evolutionary genomicists studying why sex determination keeps being reinvented would gain a predictive rule rather than a correlation; but with only tens of origin events, a statistical test is the right tool and a model is not.

ml_idea: The project considered was a classifier mapping ancestral chromosome gene content (gene counts, testis-enriched gene density, synteny block identity) to the direction of sex chromosome evolution (XY versus ZW), trained on gecko origins and tested on other amniote origins as external validation. It dies twice over: the labels and features live only in a paywalled supplement, and even complete, the dataset is roughly 22 gecko origin events plus a few dozen vertebrate ones - a sample size for a contingency-table test, not for machine learning.

effort.compute_note: Not estimated: no file was obtainable, so there was nothing to size. Rebuilding the features from scratch would require multi-species whole-genome synteny, which is not a laptop job.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count the number of independent sex chromosome origin events - the actual rows. The abstract (16 ancestral chromosomes, 11 datable origins) and the press release (22 systems, 17 ancestral chromosomes) both put it in the low tens, which kills it before any download.

verdict_reason: No data file is reachable (Science paywall, no PubMed Central copy, supplement returns 403, no accession found in Europe PMC, NCBI, Zenodo or figshare), and the dataset is roughly 22 sex chromosome origin events - tens of rows where the checklist needs hundreds. Two independent Part A failures (A1 and A5), either of which is fatal.
